topic.name: Defining Double Integrals Using Lower and Upper Riemann Sums

exampleAnswers.title: Applying the Definition of the Double Integral in Terms of Lower and Upper Riemann Sums

question.text:
Let $R = [-4,-1]\times [0,2]$ be a region in the $xy$-plane, and let $f(x,y) = 10-x-y.$ Further, let

\[ \displaystyle I = \iint\limits_R f(x,y)\,\textrm dA \]

be the unique number such that over all rectangular partitions $P$ of $R,$ we have $ L(f,P)\:\leq I \:\leq U(f,P), $ where $L(f,P)$ and $U(f,P)$ are the corresponding lower and upper Riemann sums, and

\[ U(f,P) = \sum_{i=1}^m\sum_{j=1}^n\fbox{$\phantom{AAAAA}$} \: \Delta x_i \Delta y_j\,. \]

What expression is missing from the double summation above?
question.choice5: None of the options is correct
question.explanation:
For a function $f(x,y),$ the double integral of $f$ over a rectangular region $R$ is the unique number $I$ (if it exists) such that

\[ L(f,P) \leq I \leq U(f,P), \]

over all partitions $P$ of $R,$ where the lower and upper sums respectively are given by

\begin{align*} L(f,P) &= \sum_{i=1}^m\sum_{j=1}^n m_{ij}\Delta x_i \Delta y_j\\[5pt] U(f,P) &= \sum_{i=1}^m\sum_{j=1}^n M_{ij}\Delta x_i \Delta y_j \end{align*}

and $m_{ij}$ and $M_{ij}$ are the minimum and maximum values of $f$ respectively in each subregion $R_{ij}.$

We need to compute $U(f,P).$

Notice that for all subregions $R_{ij},$ we have that

  • $f(x,y) = 10-x-y$ decreases as $x$ increases, and

  • $f(x,y) = 10-x-y$ decreases as $y$ increases.

As a result, the maximum value of $f$ in each subregion is attained when we have the smallest possible $x$ and the smallest possible $y.$ This is the value at the bottom left corner of each subregion. Therefore,

\[ M_{ij} = f(x_{i-1}, y_{j-1}) = 10-x_{i-1}-y_{j-1} \]

and the upper Riemann sum is given by

\[ U(f,P) = \sum_{i=1}^m\sum_{j=1}^n ({\color{blue}{10-x_{i-1}-y_{j-1}}})\Delta x_i \Delta y_j. \]

So, the missing expression is $10-x_{i-1}-y_{j-1}.$

exampleAnswers.title: Calculating a Double Integral Using Lower and Upper Riemann Sums

question.text:
Let $R = [2,4]\times [1,5]$ be a region in the $xy$-plane, and let $P$ be a partition of $R,$ where

\begin{align*} P_1 = \left\{x_0,x_1,\ldots, x_m\right\}, \qquad P_2 = \left\{y_0,y_1,\ldots, y_n\right\}, \qquad P = P_1\times P_2. \end{align*}

Calculate the double integral

\[ \displaystyle\iint\limits_R f(x,y) \, \textrm{d}A, \]

where $f$ is a function such that $m_{ij} = M_{ij} = 5$ for all partitions $P$ of $R,$ and $m_{ij}$ and $M_{ij}$ are the minimum and maximum values of $f$ respectively in each subregion $R_{ij}.$
question.explanation:
For a function $f(x,y),$ the double integral of $f$ over a rectangular region $R$ is the unique number $I$ (if it exists) such that

\[ L(f,P) \leq I \leq U(f,P), \]

over all partitions $P$ of $R,$ where the lower and upper sums respectively are given by

\begin{align*} L(f,P) &= \sum_{i=1}^m\sum_{j=1}^n m_{ij}\Delta x_i \Delta y_j\\[5pt] U(f,P) &= \sum_{i=1}^m\sum_{j=1}^n M_{ij}\Delta x_i \Delta y_j \end{align*}

and $m_{ij}$ and $M_{ij}$ are the minimum and maximum values of $f$ in each subregion $R_{ij}.$

Now, since $m_{ij}=M_{ij}=5,$ we obtain

\begin{align*} L(f,P) = U(f,P) &= \sum_{i=1}^m\sum_{j=1}^n 5 \, \Delta x_i \Delta y_j \\[5pt] %&= 5 \sum_{i=1}^m\sum_{j=1}^n \Delta x_i \Delta y_j \\[5pt] &= 5 \bigg( \sum_{i=1}^m \Delta x_i \bigg) \bigg( \sum_{j=1}^n \Delta y_j \bigg)\\[5pt] &= 5(4-2)(5-1)\\[5pt] &= 5\cdot 2\cdot 4\\[5pt] &=40. \end{align*}

Finally, we obtain

\[ L(f,P) = 40 \leq \iint\limits_R f(x,y)\,\textrm d A \leq 40 = U(f,P) \] which implies that \[ \iint\limits_R f(x,y)\,\textrm d A = 40. \]

Calculate the double integral \[ \iint\limits_R f(x,y) \, \textrm{d}A, \] where $f$ is a function such that $m_{ij}=M_{ij}=7$ for all partitions $P$ of $R,$ and $m_{ij}$ and $M_{ij}$ are the minimum and maximum values of $f$ respectively in each subregion $R_{ij}.$
question.explanation:
For a function $f(x,y),$ the double integral of $f$ over a rectangular region $R$ is the unique number $I$ (if it exists) such that

\[ L(f,P) \leq I \leq U(f,P), \]

over all partitions $P$ of $R,$ where the lower and upper sums respectively are given by

\begin{align*} L(f,P) &= \sum_{i=1}^m\sum_{j=1}^n m_{ij}\Delta x_i \Delta y_j\\[5pt] U(f,P) &= \sum_{i=1}^m\sum_{j=1}^n M_{ij}\Delta x_i \Delta y_j \end{align*}

and $m_{ij}$ and $M_{ij}$ are the minimum and maximum values of $f$ in each subregion $R_{ij}.$

Now, since $m_{ij}=M_{ij}=7,$ we obtain

\begin{align*} L(f,P) = U(f,P) &= \sum_{i=1}^m\sum_{j=1}^n 7 \, \Delta x_i \Delta y_j \\[5pt] %&= 7 \sum_{i=1}^m\sum_{j=1}^n \Delta x_i \Delta y_j \\[5pt] &= 7 \bigg( \sum_{i=1}^m \Delta x_i \bigg) \bigg( \sum_{j=1}^n \Delta y_j \bigg)\\[5pt] &= 7(-1-(-4))(3-0)\\[5pt] &= 7\cdot 3\cdot 3\\[5pt] &=63. \end{align*}

Finally, we obtain

\[ L(f,P) = 63 \leq \iint\limits_R f(x,y)\,\textrm d A \leq 63 = U(f,P) \] which implies that \[ \iint\limits_R f(x,y)\,\textrm d A = 63. \]

exampleAnswers.title: Calculating a Double Integral Using the Mean Value of X and Y

question.text:
Let $R = [2,5]\times [-2,2]$ be a region in the $xy$-plane, and let $f(x,y)$ be a function defined over $R.$ The lower and upper Riemann sums corresponding to an arbitrary partition $P$ of $R$ are given by

\begin{align*} L(f,P) &= \sum_{i=1}^m\sum_{j=1}^n (2y_{j-1}-2x_{i} + 1)\Delta x_i \Delta y_j, \\[5pt] U(f,P) &= \sum_{i=1}^m\sum_{j=1}^n (2y_{j}-2x_{i-1} +1)\Delta x_i \Delta y_j. \end{align*}

Using the definition of the double integral in terms of $L(f,P)$ and $U(f,P),$ compute $\displaystyle\iint\limits_R f(x,y)\,\textrm{d}A.$

Hint: You may wish to make use of the following results: \begin{align*} \sum_{i=1}^m\sum_{j=1}^n\left(x_{i-1} + x_i\right)\Delta x_i \Delta y_j = (x_m^2 - x_0^2)(y_n-y_0)\\[5pt] \sum_{i=1}^m\sum_{j=1}^n \Delta x_i \Delta y_j = (x_m - x_0)(y_n-y_0) \end{align*}
question.explanation:
For a function $f(x,y),$ the double integral of $f$ over a rectangular region $R$ is the unique number $I$ (if it exists) such that \[ L(f,P) \leq I \leq U(f,P) \] over all partitions $P$ of $R.$

First, notice that $\bar{x}_i = \dfrac 1 2 (x_{i-1}+x_i)$ will always lie between $x_{i-1}$ and $x_i$, and similarly $\bar{y}_j = \dfrac 1 2 (y_{j-1}+y_j)$ will always lie between $y_{j-1}$ and $y_j.$ Therefore, \[ {\color{red}2}y_{j-1} - {\color{blue}2}x_{i}+1 \leq {\color{red}2} \cdot \dfrac{1}{2}(y_{j-1} + y_j) - {\color{blue}2}\cdot \dfrac 1 2 (x_{i-1} + x_i)+1 \leq {\color{red}2}y_{j} - {\color{blue}2}x_{i-1} +1 \] which simplifies to \[ 2y_{j-1} - 2x_{i} +1\leq (y_{j-1} + y_j) - (x_{i-1} + x_i) + 1 \leq 2y_{j} - 2x_{i-1}+1. \]

Multiplying this by $\Delta x_i\Delta y_j$ and applying the double summation gives: \[ L(f,P) \leq \sum_{i=1}^m\sum_{j=1}^n\left[(y_{j-1} + y_j) - (x_{i-1} + x_i)+1\right]\Delta x_i \Delta y_j\leq U(f,P) \]

Separating the sums using the addition rule, we get \begin{align*} L(f,P) &\leq \sum_{i=1}^m \sum_{j=1}^n \left(y_{j-1} + y_j\right)\Delta x_i \Delta y_j \\[5pt] &\phantom{\leq}\: - \sum_{i=1}^m \sum_{j=1}^n \left(x_{i-1} + x_i\right)\Delta x_i \Delta y_j \\[5pt] &\phantom{\leq}\: + \sum_{i=1}^m \sum_{j=1}^n \Delta x_i \Delta y_j \\[5pt] &\leq U(f,P). \end{align*}

Using the hint, we get the following: \begin{align*} \sum_{i=1}^m\sum_{j=1}^n\left(x_{j-1} + x_j\right)\Delta x_i \Delta y_j & = (5^2-2^2)(2-(-2)) = 84\\[5pt] \sum_{i=1}^m\sum_{j=1}^n\left(y_{j-1} + y_j\right)\Delta x_i \Delta y_j & = (2^2-(-2)^2)(5-2) = 0 \\[5pt] \sum_{i=1}^m\sum_{j=1}^n\Delta x_i \Delta y_j & = (5-2)(2-(-2)) = 12 \end{align*}

Finally then: \begin{align*} L(f,P) \leq 0 - 84 + 12 \leq U(f,P)\qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad L(f,P) \leq -72 \leq U(f,P) \end{align*}

Therefore, we conclude that \[ \iint\limits_R f(x,y)\,\textrm d A = -72. \]

example.title: Calculating a Double Integral Using the Mean Value of X and Y

question.text:
Let $R = [0,6]\times [1,2]$ be a region in the $xy$-plane, and let $f(x,y)$ be a function defined over $R.$ The lower and upper Riemann sums corresponding to an arbitrary partition $P$ of $R$ are given by \begin{align*} L(f,P) &= \sum_{i=1}^m\sum_{j=1}^n (x_{i-1} - y_{j})\Delta x_i \Delta y_j, \\[5pt] U(f,P) &= \sum_{i=1}^m\sum_{j=1}^n (x_{i} - y_{j-1})\Delta x_i \Delta y_j. \end{align*}

Using the definition of the double integral in terms of $L(f,P)$ and $U(f,P),$ compute $\displaystyle\iint\limits_R f(x,y)\,\textrm{d}A.$

Hint: You may wish to make use of the following result: \begin{align*} \sum_{i=1}^m\sum_{j=1}^n(x_{i-1} + x_i)\Delta x_i \Delta y_j = (x_m^2 - x_0^2)(y_n-y_0) \end{align*}
question.explanation:
For a function $f(x,y),$ the double integral of $f$ over a rectangular region $R$ is the unique number $I$ (if it exists) such that \[ L(f,P) \leq I \leq U(f,P) \] over all partitions $P$ of $R.$

First, notice that $\bar{x}_i = \dfrac 1 2 (x_{i-1}+x_i)$ will always lie between $x_{i-1}$ and $x_i$, and similarly $\bar{y}_j = \dfrac 1 2 (y_{j-1}+y_j)$ will always lie between $y_{j-1}$ and $y_j.$ Therefore, \[ x_{i-1} - y_{j} \leq \dfrac{1}{2}(x_{i-1} + x_i) - \dfrac 1 2 (y_{j-1} + y_j) \leq x_{i} - y_{j-1} \]

Multiplying this by $\Delta x_i\Delta y_j$ and applying the double summation gives: \[ L(f,P) \leq \sum_{i=1}^m\sum_{j=1}^n\left[\dfrac 1 2(x_{i-1} + x_i) - \dfrac 1 2(y_{j-1} + y_j)\right]\Delta x_i \Delta y_j\leq U(f,P) \]

Separating the sums using the addition and constant multiple rules, we get \begin{align*} L(f,P) &\leq \dfrac 1 2\sum_{i=1}^m\sum_{j=1}^n(x_{i-1} + x_i)\Delta x_i \Delta y_j - \dfrac 1 2\sum_{i=1}^m\sum_{j=1}^n (y_{j-1} + y_j)\Delta x_i \Delta y_j \\[5pt] &\leq U(f,P). \end{align*}

Using the hint, we get the following: \begin{align*} \dfrac 1 2 \sum_{i=1}^m\sum_{j=1}^n(x_{i-1} + x_i)\Delta x_i \Delta y_j & = \dfrac 1 2 (6^2-0^2)(2-1) = 18 \\[5pt] \dfrac 1 2\sum_{i=1}^m\sum_{j=1}^n(y_{j-1} + y_j)\Delta x_i \Delta y_j & = \dfrac 1 2(2^2-1^2)(6-0) = 9 \end{align*}

Finally then: \begin{align*} L(f,P) \leq 18 - 9 \leq U(f,P)\qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad L(f,P) \leq 9 \leq U(f,P) \end{align*}

Therefore, we conclude that \[ \iint\limits_R f(x,y)\,\textrm d A = 9. \]

question.text:
Let $R = [0,2]\times [2,3]$ be a region in the $xy$-plane, and let $f(x,y)$ be a function defined over $R.$ The lower and upper Riemann sums corresponding to an arbitrary partition $P$ of $R$ are given by

\begin{align*} L(f,P) & = \sum_{i=1}^m\sum_{j=1}^n (8 - 2x_{i} - y_{j})\Delta x_i \Delta y_j, \\[5pt] U(f,P) &= \sum_{i=1}^m\sum_{j=1}^n (8 - 2x_{i-1} - y_{j-1})\Delta x_i \Delta y_j. \end{align*}

Using the definition of the double integral in terms of $L(f,P)$ and $U(f,P),$ compute $\displaystyle\iint\limits_R f(x,y)\,\textrm{d}A.$

Hint: You may wish to make use of the following results: \begin{align*} \sum_{i=1}^m\sum_{j=1}^n(x_{i-1} + x_i)\Delta x_i \Delta y_j = (x_m^2 - x_0^2)(y_n-y_0)\\[5pt] \sum_{i=1}^m\sum_{j=1}^n \Delta x_i \Delta y_j = (x_m - x_0)(y_n-y_0) \end{align*}
question.explanation:
For a function $f(x,y),$ the double integral of $f$ over a rectangular region $R$ is the unique number $I$ (if it exists) such that \[ L(f,P) \leq I \leq U(f,P) \] over all partitions $P$ of $R.$

First, notice that $\bar{x}_i = \dfrac 1 2 (x_{i-1}+x_i)$ will always lie between $x_{i-1}$ and $x_i$, and similarly $\bar{y}_j = \dfrac 1 2 (y_{j-1}+y_j)$ will always lie between $y_{j-1}$ and $y_j.$ Therefore, \[ 8 - {\color{blue}2}x_{i} - y_{j} \leq 8 - {\color{blue}2} \cdot \dfrac{1}{2}(x_{i-1} + x_i) - \dfrac 1 2 (y_{j-1} + y_j) \leq 8 - {\color{blue}2}x_{i-1} - y_{j-1} \] which simplifies to \[ 8 - 2x_{i} - y_{j} \leq 8- (x_{i-1} + x_i) - \dfrac 1 2(y_{j-1} + y_j) \leq 8 - 2x_{i-1} - y_{j-1}. \]

Multiplying this by $\Delta x_i\Delta y_j$ and applying the double summation gives: \[ L(f,P) \leq \sum_{i=1}^m\sum_{j=1}^n\left[8- (x_{i-1} + x_i) - \dfrac 1 2(y_{j-1} + y_j)\right]\Delta x_i \Delta y_j\leq U(f,P) \]

Separating the sums using the addition and constant multiple rules, we get \begin{align*} L(f,P) &\leq 8\sum_{i=1}^m\sum_{j=1}^n \Delta x_i \Delta y_j \\[5pt] &\phantom{\leq}\: -\sum_{i=1}^m\sum_{j=1}^n(x_{i-1} + x_i)\Delta x_i \Delta y_j \\[5pt] &\phantom{\leq}\: -\dfrac 1 2\sum_{i=1}^m\sum_{j=1}^n(y_{j-1} + y_j)\Delta x_i \Delta y_j \\[5pt] & \leq U(f,P). \end{align*}

Using the hint, we get the following: \begin{align*} \sum_{i=1}^m\sum_{j=1}^n(x_{i-1} + x_i)\Delta x_i \Delta y_j & = (2^2-0^2)(3-2) = 4 \\[5pt] \dfrac 1 2\sum_{i=1}^m\sum_{j=1}^n(y_{j-1} + y_i)\Delta x_i \Delta y_j & = \dfrac 1 2(3^2-2^2)(2-0) = 5\\[5pt] 8\sum_{i=1}^m\sum_{j=1}^n\Delta x_i \Delta y_j & = 8(2-0)(3-2) = 16 \end{align*}

Finally then: \begin{align*} L(f,P) \leq 16 - 4 - 5 \leq U(f,P)\qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad L(f,P) \leq 7 \leq U(f,P) \end{align*}

Therefore, we conclude that \[ \iint\limits_R f(x,y)\,\textrm d A = 7. \]

example.title: Calculating a Double Integral Using the Mean Value of X and Y

question.text:
Let $R = [-3,1]\times [2,4]$ be a region in the $xy$-plane, and let $f(x,y)$ be a function defined over $R.$ The lower and upper Riemann sums corresponding to an arbitrary partition $P$ of $R$ are given by \begin{align*} L(f,P) &= \sum_{i=1}^m\sum_{j=1}^n (y_{j-1}-x_{i})\Delta x_i \Delta y_j, \\[5pt] U(f,P) &= \sum_{i=1}^m\sum_{j=1}^n (y_{j}-x_{i-1})\Delta x_i \Delta y_j. \end{align*}

Using the definition of the double integral in terms of $L(f,P)$ and $U(f,P),$ compute $\displaystyle\iint\limits_R f(x,y)\,\textrm{d}A.$

Hint: You may wish to make use of the following result: \begin{align*} \sum_{i=1}^m\sum_{j=1}^n(x_{i-1} + x_i)\Delta x_i \Delta y_j = (x_m^2 - x_0^2)(y_n-y_0) \end{align*}
question.explanation:
For a function $f(x,y),$ the double integral of $f$ over a rectangular region $R$ is the unique number $I$ (if it exists) such that \[ L(f,P) \leq I \leq U(f,P) \] over all partitions $P$ of $R.$

First, notice that $\bar{x}_i = \dfrac 1 2 (x_{i-1}+x_i)$ will always lie between $x_{i-1}$ and $x_i$, and similarly $\bar{y}_j = \dfrac 1 2 (y_{j-1}+y_j)$ will always lie between $y_{j-1}$ and $y_j.$ Therefore, \[ y_{j-1} - x_{i} \leq \dfrac{1}{2}(y_{j-1} + y_j) - \dfrac 1 2 (x_{i-1} + x_i) \leq y_{j} - x_{i-1}. \]

Multiplying this by $\Delta x_i\Delta y_j$ and applying the double summation gives: \[ L(f,P) \leq \sum_{i=1}^m\sum_{j=1}^n\left[\dfrac12(y_{j-1} + y_j) - \dfrac12(x_{i-1} + x_i)\right]\Delta x_i \Delta y_j\leq U(f,P) \]

Separating the sums using the addition rule, we get \begin{align*} L(f,P) &\leq \dfrac12\sum_{i=1}^m\sum_{j=1}^n(y_{j-1} + y_j)\Delta x_i \Delta y_j - \dfrac12\sum_{i=1}^m\sum_{j=1}^n(x_{i-1} + x_i)\Delta x_i \Delta y_j \\[5pt] &\leq U(f,P). \end{align*}

Using the hint, we get the following: \begin{align*} \dfrac12 \sum_{i=1}^m\sum_{j=1}^n(x_{j-1} + x_j)\Delta x_i \Delta y_j & = \dfrac12(1^2-(-3)^2)(4-2) = -8 \\[5pt] \dfrac12 \sum_{i=1}^m\sum_{j=1}^n(y_{j-1} + y_j)\Delta x_i \Delta y_j & = \dfrac12(4^2-2^2)(1-(-3)) = 24 \end{align*}

Finally then: \begin{align*} L(f,P) \leq 24 - (-8) \leq U(f,P)\qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad L(f,P) \leq 32 \leq U(f,P) \end{align*}

Therefore, we conclude that \[ \iint\limits_R f(x,y)\,\textrm d A = 32. \]

question.text:
Let $R = [1,3]\times [-1,1]$ be a region in the $xy$-plane, and let $f(x,y)$ be a function defined over $R.$ The lower and upper Riemann sums corresponding to an arbitrary partition $P$ of $R$ are given by \begin{align*} L(f,P) &= \sum_{i=1}^m\sum_{j=1}^n (4x_{i-1} - 2y_{j}-2)\Delta x_i \Delta y_j, \\[5pt] U(f,P) &= \sum_{i=1}^m\sum_{j=1}^n (4x_{i} - 2y_{j-1}-2)\Delta x_i \Delta y_j. \end{align*}

Using the definition of the double integral in terms of $L(f,P)$ and $U(f,P),$ compute $\displaystyle\iint\limits_R f(x,y)\,\textrm{d}A.$

Hint: You may wish to make use of the following results: \begin{align*} \sum_{i=1}^m\sum_{j=1}^n(x_{i-1} + x_i)\Delta x_i \Delta y_j = (x_m^2 - x_0^2)(y_n-y_0)\\[5pt] \sum_{i=1}^m\sum_{j=1}^n \Delta x_i \Delta y_j = (x_m - x_0)(y_n-y_0) \end{align*}
question.explanation:
For a function $f(x,y),$ the double integral of $f$ over a rectangular region $R$ is the unique number $I$ (if it exists) such that \[ L(f,P) \leq I \leq U(f,P) \] over all partitions $P$ of $R.$

First, notice that $\bar{x}_i = \dfrac 1 2 (x_{i-1}+x_i)$ will always lie between $x_{i-1}$ and $x_i$, and similarly $\bar{y}_j = \dfrac 1 2 (y_{j-1}+y_j)$ will always lie between $y_{j-1}$ and $y_j.$ Therefore, \[ {\color{red}4}x_{i-1} - {\color{blue}2}y_{j} -2 \leq {\color{red}4}\cdot\dfrac{1}{2}(x_{i-1} + x_i) - {\color{blue}2}\cdot \dfrac 1 2 (y_{j-1} + y_j) - 2 \leq {\color{red}4}x_{i} - {\color{blue}2}y_{j-1} - 2 \] which simplifies to \[ 4x_{i-1} - 2y_{j} - 2 \leq 2(x_{i-1} + x_i) - (y_{j-1} + y_j) - 2 \leq 4x_{i} - 2y_{j-1} - 2. \]

Multiplying this by $\Delta x_i\Delta y_j$ and applying the double summation gives: \[ L(f,P) \leq \sum_{i=1}^m\sum_{j=1}^n\left[2(x_{i-1} + x_i) - (y_{j-1} + y_j) - 2\right]\Delta x_i \Delta y_j\leq U(f,P) \]

Separating the sums using the addition and constant multiple rules, we get \begin{align*} L(f,P) &\leq 2\sum_{i=1}^m\sum_{j=1}^n(x_{i-1} + x_i)\Delta x_i \Delta y_j \\[5pt] &\phantom{\leq}\: - \sum_{i=1}^m\sum_{j=1}^n(y_{j-1} + y_j)\Delta x_i \Delta y_j \\[5pt] &\phantom{\leq}\: -2 \sum_{i=1}^m\sum_{j=1}^n\Delta x_i \Delta y_j \\[5pt] &\leq U(f,P). \end{align*}

Using the hint, we get the following: \begin{align*} 2\sum_{i=1}^m\sum_{j=1}^n(x_{i-1} + x_i)\Delta x_i \Delta y_j & = 2(3^2-1^2)(1-(-1)) = 32 \\[5pt] \sum_{i=1}^m\sum_{j=1}^n(y_{j-1} + y_j)\Delta x_i \Delta y_j & = (1^2-(-1)^2)(3-1) = 0 \\[5pt] 2\sum_{i=1}^m\sum_{j=1}^n \Delta x_i \Delta y_j & = 2(3-1)(1-(-1)) = 8 \end{align*}

Finally then: \begin{align*} L(f,P) \leq 32 - 0 - 8 \leq U(f,P)\qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad L(f,P) \leq 24 \leq U(f,P) \end{align*}

Therefore, we conclude that \[ \iint\limits_R f(x,y)\,\textrm d A = 24. \]
